tasks.short: Review incoming geographic data for currency and quality.

steps.what: Open the incoming layer and read its documentation.
Check currency and completeness of required fields, dates and geometry.
Judge accuracy, usefulness and quality of the documented content.
Record the review result and defects in the geographic store.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads the geographic layer in {OTHER} and drafts a completeness list of missing fields, stale dates and invalid geometry. The GIS technician still judges accuracy, usefulness and quality, and she records that review in {OTHER}. The job does not decide whether the layer is fit to keep.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each layer used a different field list, so one completeness rule could not be configured for all of them.
tasks.enabler_now: The attributes already sit in the geographic store, so a query can test required fields, dates and geometry without reading free text.
tasks.still_hard: Usefulness and accuracy of the content still need her judgement. A layer with no field schema falls back to her.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell that a complete, current layer is still the wrong content for the question.
tasks.altitude: The field, date and geometry scan no longer fills the middle of the review. She still decides what is fit to keep and she still writes the review record.

reach.task: Define the required-field contract for a subject database
reach.learn: Which attributes a layer must carry before a completeness check is meaningful

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a scheduled query can flag missing required attributes, stale source dates and invalid geometry on a structured geographic layer. No cited product in this digest performs that check.

assumptions: The actor on every step is the GIS technician. The machine appears only as the future of the completeness check.
Contract: layer id, required field names, source date and a geometry-valid flag. The producer is the load that wrote the layer. If the schema is missing she builds the completeness list by hand.
Test the geographic store's own field rules before adding a custom job. Store runtime is not her labour.
Rule upkeep is the four hours below. She still records the review herself, so there is no separate filing step.
unknowns: Whether her geographic store exposes field rules through an interface.
What share of incoming layers already carry a required-field list.
research_questions: What share of incoming layers already carry a required-field list and a source date?

already_counted.description: Judging accuracy, usefulness and quality stays in a3.

incremental.description: Keep the required-field and date rules current for each layer type.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When half the incoming layers have no field schema she still checks those by hand, so the saved share falls near 14. When schemas are stable the field and date check covers most of that scan and the net is near 28.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Produce layers and maps with a spatial analysis procedure.

steps.what: Read the request and the source layers for the spatial analysis.
Choose the spatial analysis procedure for this request.
Run that procedure and produce layers, maps or tables.
Review the produced layers, maps, tables or reports for meaning.
Write the accepted layers into the geographic information systems.

tasks.design: After the GIS technician chooses a named procedure, a job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} runs it against source layers in {OTHER} and produces draft layers, maps or tables. She reviews their meaning and writes the accepted layers into {OTHER}. The job does not choose the procedure and does not publish outside the organisation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each map used a different procedure, so the chain could not be configured once.
tasks.enabler_now: A named procedure with fixed parameters can run as a job once she has chosen it.
tasks.still_hard: Novel spatial questions, and whether the result means what the requester needs, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows when a technically correct overlay is the wrong map.
tasks.altitude: Repeated procedures no longer take the afternoon. She still chooses the procedure, reviews the meaning and writes the accepted layers.

reach.task: Publish a curated dataset for reuse
reach.learn: Which produced layers are stable enough to expose as a shared dataset

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a configured geoprocessing chain can produce a draft layer from a named procedure and source layers. No digest product does spatial analysis.

assumptions: The actor on every step is the GIS technician. The machine appears only as the future of the procedure run.
Contract: procedure name, source layer ids and the parameter values she set in the chosen procedure. If the procedure is not in the configured list she produces the layer herself.
She writes the accepted layers. That save is her step, not a machine filing step.
Procedure-parameter upkeep is the four hours below.
unknowns: How many of her daily products are a repeated named procedure rather than a one-off analysis.
research_questions: Which spatial procedures recur often enough to configure, and which stay one-off?

already_counted.description: Choosing the procedure and reviewing the result stay in b2 and b4.

incremental.description: Keep named procedure parameters current when source layers change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A day of one-off spatial questions leaves the procedure run in her hands, so saving is near 8. A day of repeated buffers and clips lets the job produce the draft layers, so saving is near 20.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain and modify existing geographic databases.

steps.what: Read the existing geographic databases she must maintain.
Decide how to modify rows that are missing or need judgement.
Prepare stated field updates for the other existing rows.
Review proposed updates before they modify the databases.
Write the accepted updates into the geographic information systems.

tasks.design: The GIS technician decides the modify. A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts field updates for the other rows of the geographic database in {OTHER}. She reviews that draft and writes the accepted updates herself. No agent writes the database.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each modify mixed judgement with bulk edits, so the bulk part was not separated.
tasks.enabler_now: A stated field update is structured and can be drafted as a change list before anyone writes.
tasks.still_hard: Missing values, and whether the modify is the right one, stay with her. Undoing a bad write takes effort, so she still writes.
tasks.human_edge: She sees when a clean update would break a layer someone else relies on.
tasks.altitude: Repeated attribute fills become a draft she reviews. She still decides the modify and she still writes the databases.

reach.task: Set key rules for a subject database
reach.learn: Which geographic tables must not take a bulk field update

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a stated field rule can draft row updates for a structured geographic database. No digest product maintains a geographic database.
An agent deleted a production database despite instructions, so this design does not let an agent write the database.

assumptions: The actor on every step is the GIS technician. The machine appears only as the future draft of stated field updates.
Contract: table name, key field, column, new value and her modify instruction. Rows with missing values are skipped and stay in her decision.
She writes the accepted updates. The draft is not a commit.
Rule-list upkeep is the four hours below. An agent must not write this database.
unknowns: What share of daily modifies are repeated field fills rather than one-off repairs.
research_questions: Which geographic tables are safe for a drafted field update, and which must stay fully manual?

already_counted.description: Deciding the modify and reviewing the draft stay in c2 and c4.

incremental.description: Keep the allowed field-update rules current for each geographic table.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A day of repairs and missing values stays with her, so saving is near 8. A day of repeated attribute fills lets the draft cover that prepare step, so saving is near 18.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select cartographic elements for a presentation.

steps.what: Read the information the presentation must carry.
Select the cartographic elements needed for an effective presentation.
Place only the scale bar, north arrow or source line she selected.
Arrange the remaining cartographic elements so the presentation reads clearly.

tasks.design: The GIS technician selects the cartographic elements. A layout template in {OTHER} then places the scale bar, north arrow and source line she named. She arranges the presentation. The template does not choose elements and does not send the map outside.
tasks.previous_blocker: Element choice and placement were one manual layout, so the repeated frame items were not separated.
tasks.enabler_now: Scale bar, north arrow and source line are the same on most maps, so a template can place them after she selects them.
tasks.still_hard: Which elements the reader needs, and whether the presentation is effective, stay a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell that a complete frame still misleads the reader.
tasks.altitude: Selection stays her decision. Standard frame items no longer take the last minutes. Her decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Set presentation standards for stored documents
reach.learn: Which element rules belong in the template and which stay in her selection

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a layout template can place a scale bar, north arrow and source line once those elements are selected. Choosing cartographic elements is not something the digest products do.

assumptions: The actor on every step is the GIS technician. The machine appears only as the future placement of frame items she already selected.
Contract: the element names she selected, limited to scale bar, north arrow and source line. The producer is her selection. Anything else she arranges herself.
The template does not publish the map. House-style upkeep is the two hours below.
unknowns: Whether her geographic tool already has a layout template she can configure without new code.
research_questions: How often is the frame only a scale bar, north arrow and source line, and how often is the legend custom?

already_counted.description: Selecting and arranging cartographic elements stay in d2 and d4.

incremental.description: Update the layout template when the house style for the scale bar, north arrow or source line changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A presentation with a custom legend saves near 2, because she still places almost everything. A standard frame, after she has selected those items, saves near 6.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week keeps the judgement: whether data is fit, which procedure to run, which modify is safe, and which cartographic elements a presentation needs. Repeated field checks, named procedures and standard map furniture take less of the day. She still writes layers and database updates herself.
skills_to_grow: Write the required-field and date rules so a check can run without her
Name spatial procedures and parameters so a job can produce a draft layer
Separate a bulk field update from a modify that needs judgement
role.ambitious_version: She could publish a checked layer catalogue the same day a scientist asks, once currency, procedure and database rules are configured. That wider service is not this design. This design only drafts the repeatable parts and leaves the judgement and the writes with her.

job.title: Geographic Information Systems Technologists and Technicians
